requirement:
HC represents a GitHub issue by a stable owner, repository, and issue-number
identity. Reading the node supplies the issue's title, opening post, and
open/closed status as one snapshot. HC computes its fingerprint and formatted
text from that supplied snapshot through `Domain`.

For illustration:

```rust,ignore
struct GithubIssueContents {
    title: String,
    opening_post: String,
    status: IssueStatus,
}

enum IssueStatus {
    Open,
    Closed,
}
```
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes` has several obligations:
- A GitHub issue is represented by a stable owner, repository and issue-number identity.
- Reading the node supplies the title, opening post and open/closed status as one snapshot.
- The fingerprint and formatted text are computed from that snapshot through `Domain`.

The `references` tool shows no `{test}` or `{impl}` sites for this requirement. A text search of `src` for GitHub issue contents types turned up nothing for the SDK. The GitHub code in `src/github.rs` (`GithubIssues` and its tests) serves `requirements.authoring.github_reads`, not SDK graph nodes. So no test checks any of these obligations, and that is a gap.

The gap is acknowledged. `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` carries a `{fixme}` on `requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes`. It names `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26`, which is open. Its body describes the same gap: stable owner/repository/number identity and retained title/opening-post/status contents have no implementation or tests. The acknowledgment is on the subject itself, so the gap is covered, and the only issue to list is `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26`.
